A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same four-task patent-analysis survey despite the changed title. Text, equations, figures, tables, and v3 Appendix A are readable and support reliable matching. v2 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 is a literature survey. Its performance tables report results attributed to cited studies; no original experiments or empirical reanalysis are reported.

after.justification: v3 remains a literature survey, including its appendix. Tables 8–9 reproduce cited results, while the search account and descriptive comparison tables do not report original empirical evaluations.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an executable algorithm or model. The additional language models and expanded taxonomy in v3 describe existing research, rather than introduce components of a method proposed by this survey.

E1.justification: Neither survey itself uses datasets for training or evaluation. The IMPACT catalogue entry and additional generation and retrieval studies expand literature coverage. Cross-jurisdictional retrieval is proposed as future work, not evaluated.

E2.justification: Neither version benchmarks a proposed method against baselines. Newly reviewed methods are literature additions. Jiang and Setchi remain in v3 Table 2 even though their rows containing no scores disappear from the retrieval-results table.

E3.justification: No evaluation protocol is conducted or revised by the survey. Metrics for retained result entries remain unchanged. Added descriptions of published training configurations and corpus sizes document other studies rather than establish rerun or redesigned evaluations.

E4.justification: Neither version presents its own ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies. New Table 11 summarizes published multimodal architectures and corpus sizes; the additional discussion does not constitute a supplementary experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions present literature scores without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v3 does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 Tables 8–9 add Bekamiri's precision/recall/F1 of 0.67/0.71/0.66 and Lo's mAP of 0.69. Althammer's paired results in v2 Table 5 become a single reported set. Section 3.4 adds findings about general-purpose models outperforming patent-specific models. Most retained scores are unchanged; these literature additions do not establish comparable-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The classification, retrieval, and generation formulations move from v2 Section 2.1 to v3 Appendix A.3. The explicit multi-label vector and revised input wording clarify existing formulations without changing their mathematical substance. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central four-task survey and taxonomy contributions remain. v3 reframes the remit around NLP, PLMs/LLMs, and multimodal AI, and emphasizes capturing recent task-specific trends beyond earlier surveys instead of primarily distinguishing its inclusion of both images and text.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive qualifications about cross-study comparability, interprets general-purpose models' advantages, and expands discussion of factual and legal evaluation, RAG, expert feedback, and cross-jurisdictional retrieval. Section 6 adds limitations concerning expert dependence and worker displacement. Conversely, much of v2's dataset-curation and explainability agenda is removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds survey-repository access information and search sources, keywords, screening procedures, and inclusion scope in Appendix A.2. Table 11 newly documents fusion strategies and corpus sizes. Some information is lost: Jiang's CLEF-IP/USPTO and Setchi's IPO dataset labels in v2 Table 6 become dashes in v3 Table 2.

R1.justification: The literature review expands substantially through 2024, particularly from two GPT-2 generation studies to nine studies covering specification drafting, patent-specific models, feedback-based training, and multi-agent drafting. Classification and multimodal retrieval also gain studies. The introduction engages four additional prior surveys, while Lee's 2023 generative-model evaluation reference is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively reframed, with PLM terminology replacing many earlier LLM labels. Generation and discussion subsections are reorganized. Background formulations, datasets, results, and other applications move into an organized appendix, and separate limitations and ethics sections are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn and expanded, while the unchanged Figure 2 moves to the appendix. Tables are extensively relocated and restructured, including dataset columns beside results. New Tables 4, 5, and 11 summarize language-model trends, generation studies, and multimodal fusion.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the survey's usefulness through a more informative generation review, newly documented literature selection, and explicit caution about cross-study comparisons. These gains are tempered by lost dataset details and broad performance assertions: Section 3.2.4's highest-mAP statement is not established by Table 9's heterogeneous comparisons. The net improvement is useful but limited.
